title: Carbon monoxide poisoning: talking to the family
stem: Relatives' room. Ms Wong, 23, was found in a sealed room with a burnt charcoal burner. Her GCS was 7 and she has been intubated. COHb was 35%. Her mother has just arrived. Explain her condition and the plan, including hyperbaric oxygen.
notes:
Checked against TOXBASE, the Undersea and Hyperbaric Medical Society indications, the Cochrane review of hyperbaric oxygen for CO poisoning (2011) and Weaver et al. (NEJM 2002).

CO binds haemoglobin (~240 times more than oxygen), shifts the dissociation curve left, and poisons cytochrome oxidase. Treatment: 100% oxygen (half-life of COHb about 5 hours in air, 60–90 minutes on 100%, about 20–30 minutes at 2.5–3 ATA). Hyperbaric oxygen is considered for loss of consciousness, neurological signs, COHb over 25% (over 15–20% in pregnancy), cardiac ischaemia or severe acidosis, aiming to reduce delayed neurological sequelae; evidence is mixed (Weaver 2002 positive; Cochrane 2011 inconclusive). Risks: ear and sinus barotrauma (myringotomy in intubated patients), pulmonary barotrauma, oxygen toxicity seizures, claustrophobia, transfer risks. Absolute contraindication: untreated pneumothorax. Relative/drug contraindications: bleomycin exposure, doxorubicin, cisplatin, disulfiram.

Deliberate self-poisoning: psychiatric assessment once recovered; screen for co-ingestion (paracetamol, alcohol); check others at the scene.

Your notes match on indications, complications, preparation and procedure; they omit untreated pneumothorax, the main absolute contraindication.

steps.label: Talk to Mrs Wong
steps.hint: Introduce, what happened, why the breathing tube, hyperbaric oxygen, questions, support.

opts.t: I'm Dr Lee, looking after your daughter. Please sit down. She was found in a room with burning charcoal; she breathed in carbon monoxide gas, which stops blood carrying oxygen. She was very drowsy, so we put a breathing tube in to protect her airway and give her pure oxygen.
opts.mark: Explains what happened and why she was intubated

opts.t: She is seriously ill but her heart and blood pressure are stable. The main worry is damage to the brain, which can appear days or weeks later. We'd like to give her oxygen in a pressure chamber — hyperbaric oxygen — which may reduce that risk.
opts.mark: Explains prognosis and the rationale for HBOT, including delayed sequelae

opts.t: It's generally safe. The pressure can hurt the ears, so an ENT doctor will make tiny holes in her eardrums that heal later. Rarely it can cause seizures from oxygen, or lung injury. A doctor and nurse will be with her throughout; usually 1–3 sessions of about 90 minutes.
opts.r: OK. What do you need from me?
opts.mark: Explains risks and preparation (myringotomy) and the procedure

turns.line: OK. What do you need from me?

opts.t: Has she ever had chemotherapy, lung problems like a collapsed lung, or take medicines like disulfiram? And did she have any other medicines at home she might have taken?
opts.r: No chemo. She had depression last year — sertraline.

opts.t: Thank you for telling me. Once she's awake, the mental health team will see her. I'll ask our social worker to support you, and I'll update you as soon as anything changes.
opts.mark: Plans psychiatric assessment and supports the family

qs.q: Why is SpO2 unreliable in CO poisoning?
wrong: CO causes intense peripheral vasoconstriction in the fingers
It is reliable at COHb below 30%

qs.q: Main aim of HBOT in CO poisoning?
wrong: Speed healing of associated skin burns and smoke injury
Prevent aspiration pneumonia in the unconscious

qs.q: A threshold commonly used for HBOT in pregnancy?

badge.name: Pressure Chamber
badge.flavor: 100% oxygen now, HBOT for the brain, pneumothorax excluded, family supported.

cards.q: CO affinity for haemoglobin compared with oxygen?

options: Loss of consciousness or neuro signs
Headache alone with a COHb of 5% in a smoker
Hypoglycaemia in diabetic patients on insulin

cards.q: Drug that makes HBOT hazardous (lung toxicity)?
Delayed neurological sequelae after CO appear…
options: Never, if the COHb normalises quickly
Discharge once the COHb is normal
